question.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing term with a coefficient of zero, as follows:

$$
2{x}^{4}-11{x}^{2}+2x+1=2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-11{x}^{2}+2x+1
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,-x-3 \\  & -2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-11{x}^{2}+2x+1\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{4}-6{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,6{x}^{3}-11{x}^{2}+x+1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{6{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}+0x+3}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,7{x}^{2}+x-2\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, 

- the quotient is $-x-3,$ and

- the remainder is $7{x}^{2}+x-2.$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{2{x}^{4}-11{x}^{2}+2x+1}{-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-1}=-x-3+\frac{7{x}^{2}+x-2}{-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}-1}.
$$
